page.layout: Top: two medallion portraits with their legends, one at left and one at right. Below them: one column of running text, with no margin notes and no notes under the text. Running head at top; page number at top left.

main_text.l: PHENIS EVROPA FIL.
MINOS CRE.R.[?]
EVROPA Agenoris Phœnicum regis filia fuit, quam
Iuppiter fingitur in formam bouis rapuisse, ac per mare in Cre-
tam trānsuexisse[?]: ex qua tres genuerit liberos, Minoem, Rhada-
manthum, Sarpedonem. Vide Diodo.Sicu.lib.5.Ouid.li.2.Me-
tamor. circa finem. Interpretatur fabulam Palephatus de Cre-
tensi quodam, cui nomen erat Taurus, qui Europam captiuam
abduxerit.
Ab hac Europa, fertur tertia orbis pars denominata, quan-
quam non assentiat Herodotus, qui neminem cōpertum habe-
re dicat, vnde id tertiæ orbis parti nomen datum. Vide Hero-
dotum lib.4.
MINOS, Iouis Asterij & Europæ filius, anno à creatione
mundi 2710. ante Christum natum 1252. classem compara-
uit, mare obtinuit, & insularum Cycladū dominus primus, in
earū plerisq; colonias posuit, Caribus eiectis, filiósq; suos con-
stituit principes: latrones è mari sustulit. Thucyd.in præfatione
historiæ suæ. Hic omnium cōsensu habitus est vir iustus, & pro-
batæ vitæ, tradunt persuasisse primùm scriptis vti legibus, fin-
xisse autem eas Mercurij datas præcepto, autore Ioue. Diodor.
Sicul.lib.2.& 6. De huius Sapientia. vide Diony.Halica.lib.2.in
gestis Numæ. Volater.lib.33.sic ait: Minos certè ob summam iustitiam,

l.i: post mortem iudex apud inferos dictus est, vnà cum Rhadamantho

main_text.l: ANDROGEVS, Minoïs filius, præclaræ indolis ado-
lescens, ab Athenien-sibus, quòd in athletica superasset, occidi-
tur: idque causa belli extitit. Volater.lib.33.

page.notes: The two medallion legends are read from the curved inscriptions. The right-hand legend's last word ("CRE.R.") is unclear. The phrase after "trā" in the first paragraph is uncertain: the mark over the vowel may be a macron or tilde, and the word is marked [?]. Long s has been rendered as plain s throughout. Printed u and v have been changed to u and v per the rules, in the running head and text. The Greek-letter-free text contains no Greek or Hebrew on this page.
